note: Attacker-controlled morx font data: the end-of-text state-table entry for (state 0, CLASS_END_OF_TEXT) carries currentInsertIndex=0 (not 0xFFFF), so the current-insertion path is taken exactly when the state machine has consumed all text glyphs (buffer->idx == buffer->len).
Entry flags carry CurrentInsertCount=1, so one glyph will be inserted after the (missing) current glyph; the insertion glyph array is validated in-bounds by the sanitizer.
CurrentInsertBefore is clear, so before=false and the copy-current-glyph-then-skip branch (buffer->copy_glyph(); buffer->skip_glyph();) is executed.

Root cause: copy_glyph() is invoked without checking that a current glyph exists (buffer->idx < buffer->len). At end of text idx==len, so the copy reads one-past-the-end glyph info and the uninitialized glyph (including its glyph id) enters the output buffer.

info[len] is uninitialized memory (within the allocated buffer but beyond len); the whole glyph info struct, including the codepoint/glyph id used later for advance lookup, is copied to the output buffer.

After the state machine finishes, the output buffer (which now contains the uninitialized glyph at index len-1) is swapped in as the buffer's glyph info; buffer->len becomes 20 and positioning runs over all glyphs including the uninitialized one.
hb_ot_position_default feeds every output glyph's codepoint into the horizontal advance lookup; for the final glyph this codepoint is the uninitialized glyph id produced by the morx insertion.
The uninitialized glyph id is used as the key of the hmtx advance-width lookup.
Sink: the uninitialized glyph id is branched on in the advance-width lookup; MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value here.
